report.source_text: The CT scan revealed the presence of a predominantly fat‐containing mass with soft tissue components, measuring approximately 13 × 23 × 15 cm. This mass appeared to originate from the anterior mediastinum and extended into the right hemithorax, without a clearly evident shift of the heart and mediastinum to the left. The lesion did not reach below the diaphragm. The lower lobe of right lung exhibited almost complete collapse (Figure 2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old male presented with chest pain and signs of right-sided lung compromise after a car accident. A CT scan revealed a large anterior mediastinal mass (13x23x15 cm) originating from the anterior mediastinum and extending into the right hemithorax, causing almost complete collapse of the right lower lung lobe. The mass was entirely excised via right thoracotomy. Histopathological examination confirmed the mass as thymolipoma, showing mature adipose tissue with islands of non-neoplastic thymic epithelial cells. The patient experienced no postoperative complications and was discharged in excellent condition on the 11th day following surgery.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with chest pain and physical signs of right-sided lung compromise after a car accident.

CT scan revealed a large (13x23x15 cm) predominantly fat-containing mass with soft tissue components originating from the anterior mediastinum, extending into the right hemithorax, and causing almost complete collapse of the right lower lung lobe.
The mediastinal mass was entirely excised through a right thoracotomy.
Histopathological examination of the excised lesion confirmed thymolipoma, characterized by mature adipose tissue containing islands of non-neoplastic thymic epithelial cells.
The patient had an excellent postoperative recovery with no complications and was discharged on the 11th day.
